extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and institutional legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on designing and implementing grievance procedures to address sex discrimination and sex-based harassment under Title IX across K-12 and postsecondary settings, including procedural protections, flexibility for age-appropriate processes, interaction with other civil rights laws, and when emergency actions are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt resolution of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must address complaints of sex discrimination and sex-based harassment “prompt[ly].” (§§106.45(a)(1), 106.46(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects assertions that the procedures will unnecessarily delay resolution. Promptness is required while still providing equitable process. The preamble notes modifications from the 2020 amendments to address stakeholder concerns about lengthy procedures, particularly in K-12 contexts (87 FR 41457, 41459).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to remove respondent or place on leave during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may remove a respondent from its education program or activity on an emergency basis or place an employee respondent on administrative leave during grievance procedures (see §106.44(h) and §106.44(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removals and administrative leave are permitted in certain circumstances to address threats to safety or the educational environment while grievance procedures proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of confidential resources, supportive measures, and informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators must offer and coordinate supportive measures, and, if available and appropriate, offer informal resolution processes to mitigate deterrents to filing complaints (§106.44(f)(1)(ii),(iv),(g),(k)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes complainants may avoid formal grievance procedures; offering confidential resources and informal resolution can reduce deterrence. Informal resolution is discretionary and may be appropriate in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures should not be unduly quasi-judicial or adversarial; allow flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures should be structured so they are usable by non-attorneys and not overly mimic criminal or civil legal systems, but must still provide necessary safeguards and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules permit recipients discretion to create processes more or less adversarial (e.g., whether to hold live hearings (§106.46(g)) and how parties/witnesses are questioned (§§106.45(g), 106.46(f))). The Department agrees with commenters favoring less legalism but maintains that procedures must still promote nondiscrimination and fair fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach reliable factual determinations promptly and equitably
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must be designed to reach reliable factual determinations and do so promptly and equitably to ensure compliance with Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are required to balance fairness and reliability; the Department emphasizes the necessity of procedures that can determine whether sex discrimination occurred and, if so, identify remedies and sanctions while complying with due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and alignment with other civil rights laws
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations are limited to Title IX and do not impose new requirements for Title VI, Section 504, or the ADA; recipients must comply with all applicable regulations and may align grievance procedures across statutes where appropriate (see discussion of §106.44(a) and 34 CFR 104.7(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single complaint can raise allegations on multiple bases; if allegations relate to sex discrimination they may be handled under Title IX procedures, while non-sex allegations must be handled in accordance with other applicable laws. Recipients may choose to use a single process provided it complies with relevant standards under each law.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-12-specific adaptations: developmentally appropriate and less complex procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures for elementary and secondary schools must account for the younger student population, including allowing less complex procedures (e.g., oral complaints without signatures) and being developmentally appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents, guardians, or authorized representatives have a legal right to be present and assist minors in K-12 grievance procedures (§106.6(g)). The Department declined to require live hearings at the K-12 level and permits flexibility in communication and terminology to match students' maturity and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize retraumatization of minors and coordinate with child-abuse expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should avoid repeatedly questioning minor complainants and may consult or partner with organizations experienced in trauma-informed investigations (e.g., child advocacy centers, multidisciplinary teams) consistent with §106.44(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarifies recipients are not required to repeatedly question minors and may use existing processes or partnerships to reduce trauma; recipients also retain discretion in communicating terms and processes to minors and parents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing state/local processes if they satisfy §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use existing processes (such as State anti-bullying or student-discipline procedures) to investigate and resolve Title IX complaints if those processes satisfy the requirements of §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a uniform Federal standard is required for Title IX compliance, recipients do not have to create separate procedures when existing procedures meet §106.45 requirements. The Department believes a uniform standard is necessary for consistent enforcement but preserves recipients' flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX applicability to employees and interaction with Title VII/collective bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX applies to employees as well as students; recipients must implement grievance procedures consistent with §106.45 for employees, and postsecondary institutions additionally must implement §106.46 for student-involved sex-based harassment where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects the view that Title VII or collective bargaining preclude Title IX application. Recipients must comply with both Title IX and other employment laws; if conflicts arise, recipients must fulfill Title IX obligations (§106.6(b)). Existing employee grievance procedures may be used if they do not conflict with §§106.45 or 106.46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline procedural protections required in grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include baseline standards to ensure fairness: equitable treatment of parties; decisionmakers free of bias or conflicts of interest; adequate notice and timeframes; adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation; opportunity for parties to present evidence; and guidance for assessing evidence and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These baseline protections (summarized from the July 2022 NPRM and preamble) are intended to standardize minimum due-process and reliability features across recipients; many institutions may already have similar protections in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to present and respond to evidence and witnesses; notice before discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide notice of allegations (§106.45(c)); equal opportunity to present fact witnesses and relevant evidence (§106.45(f)(2)); equal opportunity to access and respond to relevant evidence (§106.45(f)(4)); and compliance with grievance procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions (§106.45(h)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific procedural requirements mirror Supreme Court precedents on student discipline (e.g., Goss) and are intended to ensure basic notice-and-hearing protections are preserved in Title IX grievance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit questioning to relevant and not otherwise impermissible matters
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing credibility, questions asked of parties and witnesses must be relevant and not otherwise impermissible under §§106.2 and 106.45(b)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should ensure decisionmaker questions respect relevance and statutory limits to avoid impermissible inquiry, particularly with minors and sensitive allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients need not defer exclusively to law enforcement; Title IX remedies are distinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Serious allegations (e.g., rape, sexual assault) do not automatically require exclusive handling by law enforcement; Title IX requires recipients to evaluate and, as necessary, address and remedy sex discrimination within the educational program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX enforcement and remedies (e.g., schedule or housing changes, access to extracurriculars, disciplinary sanctions under institutional codes) are distinct from criminal or civil redress; recipients are often uniquely positioned to provide immediate noncriminal remedies.
